hints.title: Distinct Sequence Gap Obstacle
hints.text: The sequence contains n distinct numbers taken from 0 to n, leaving exactly one absent. How can arithmetic sum or bitwise cancellation reveal the missing term in linear time without extra memory?

hints.title: Gauss Formula Invariant
hints.text: The expected sum of integers from 0 to n is n * (n + 1) // 2. The difference between this expected sum and the sum of elements is the missing number.

hints.title: Arithmetic Reduction Procedure
hints.text: Compute total = n * (n + 1) // 2 where n is len(nums). Subtract each element in nums from total. The remaining value is the missing number.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Direct sum computation across N elements in O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Sorting takes O(N log N) time and boolean frequency tables allocate O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Closed-form Gauss sum eliminates auxiliary array allocations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Mentioning both arithmetic sum and XOR cancellation to avoid integer overflow in fixed-width languages.
